column1: # Large search certificates that are not stored in the repository; regenerate with  code/regen_cert.sh NAME  (or  all).
# One row per certificate.  Columns:
#   name         certificate name: the Lean modules are lean/Erdos634/Refl/M<name>Inst.lean, M<name>Data<i>.lean,
#                (M<name>SoundP<j>.lean,) M<name>Sound.lean
#   instance     name of the search run (file names under rust/mrv2/out)
#   tile         side lengths of the tile, in the order given to both programs
#   target       side lengths of the target triangle, in the mrv2 orientation (base, right side, left side)
#   N            number of tiles
#   mode, la     branching order and lookahead of the float search rust/mrv2
#   nodes        number of nodes of the float refutation tree written by rust/mrv2 (field CERT= of its output line,
#                nogood subtrees included).  The exact replay checks this tree node by node.  For EQ135 the tree is
#                restricted at the root and replayed by rust/certgenx in mirror mode; the exact certificate checked
#                by the Lean kernel then has 1,326,256 nodes (the number stated in the paper), against 1,822,966 here.
#   tree_bytes, tree_sha256   size and SHA-256 of the tree file
#   lean_files, lean_bytes    number and total size of the generated Lean modules
#   lean_sha256  SHA-256 of the concatenation Inst, Data0, Data1, ..., SoundP0, SoundP1, ..., Sound
#   gen          (optional) generator: empty = rust/certgenm; certgenm+split:<PER> = rust/certgenm, then
#                code/split_sound.py cuts M<name>Sound.lean into parts of PER theorems; certgenx:<mirror>:<root slots>
#                = rust/certgenx (streaming; soundness in parts), with the search restricted at the root to the given
#                slots (MRV_ROOTSLOTS, MRV_ROOTTREE=1) and the other root placements refuted by Refl.sound_mirror.
